text:
Situation: Potassium chloride is on FDA's drug shortage list with a "To Be Discontinued" status posted 2021-11-02. Corvale East holds 2.7 days of 29.8 g/1000 mL 50 mL bags and 8.9 days of 14.9 g/100 mL injection. Corvale General holds 16.4 days of the 29.8 g/1000 mL bags and 9.7 days of 14.9 g/100 mL injection. Corvale Lakeside holds 6.1 days of 750 mg tablets and 19.2 days of 14.9 g/100 mL injection.

Why (FDA record): FDA lists potassium chloride as To Be Discontinued with an initial posting date of 2021-11-02. Baxter's plant (FEI 1416980) received OAI classifications ending 2024-08-01 and 2026-04-02. Hospira, Inc.'s plant (FEI 1021343) received OAI classifications in 2010 and 2011, with a Warning Letter issued 2010-04-12.

Our position: Internal transfers can stabilize Corvale East's critical 29.8 g/1000 mL bag supply without dropping any site below two weeks. Tablet transfers can extend Corvale Lakeside to two weeks. Purchasing from ICU Medical Inc. is viable as it is not on FDA's shortage list today.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 31 bags of 29.8 g/1000 mL, 50 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — approved by pharmacy director (transfer request).
2. Transfer 18 tablets of 750 mg from Corvale East to Corvale Lakeside — approved by pharmacy director (transfer request).
3. Transfer 19 units of 14.9 g/100 mL, 250 mL from Corvale Lakeside to Corvale East — approved by pharmacy director (transfer request).
4. Purchase potassium chloride from ICU Medical Inc. — approved by buyer.

Not recommended: Transfer 18 tablets of 750 mg from Corvale General to Corvale Lakeside (option 3) because Corvale East can supply the tablets while maintaining its own two-week buffer.
